about: Generated by scripts/build_kanji.js. Radicals ordered by how many kanji in the verified curriculum they file (most useful first). Sample words come from the curriculum first; Kanji alive examples only fill gaps. The reading used in each sample is computed against KANJIDIC2 readings (allowing regular sound changes) — "special" means the word has a reading that cannot be split into the kanji's listed readings (e.g. 今日 きょう).

radicals.name: Kanji alive — Japanese radicals, CC BY 4.0

examples.name: Kanji alive — kanji data (example words), CC BY 4.0

rule.name: Tae Kim — Kanji (on-yomi in compounds, kun-yomi alone / with okurigana; sound changes; special readings)

rule.on: In compounds of two or more kanji (熟語) a kanji is usually read with its 音読み (on-yomi, the Chinese-derived reading): 水道 すいどう.
rule.kun: Standing alone, or followed by kana (okurigana) as in verbs and adjectives, a kanji is usually read with its 訓読み (kun-yomi, the native Japanese reading): 水 みず, 食べる たべる.
rule.changes: In compounds the first sound can change (h→b/p, k→g, s→z, t→d) and つ/く/ち/き can become っ: 一本 いっぽん, 手紙 てがみ.
rule.special: Some words have special readings that have nothing to do with the single kanji (今日 きょう). These are learned as whole words.
